properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Raised by Anthony asking how CI and regression testing here could be improved, 2026-09-21.

THE OBSERVATION. Every one of the ~48 gates runs the binary built from this commit against data produced by this commit. But reflow2 is installed in other projects — flo2, bhome, hxm_program, dev_storyflow — and the defects those projects actually report are VERSION-SKEW defects, not same-version defects:
· 853 edges "gained a field on import" — root-caused to an older binary importing a newer document and injecting a stale schema default. Nothing on import compared the document's version with the binary's, and no gate could have caught it because no gate has ever run two versions against each other.
· A type removal locked every existing graph out until migrated, which needed the first upgrade note whose action is REQUIRED of every consumer.
· Two releases looked complete and shipped no container image, because the cut verified assets off the release object and the image is not an asset.

There is one gate near this — a committed export must survive export, import and re-export — but it is a round-trip at ONE version. The skew axis is untested.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN, and they are additive rather than exclusive:
(a) A GOLDEN-EXPORT CORPUS: keep a small set of exports taken at past releases (v0.50, v0.55, v0.60) and require that today's binary imports each one, reports its age, and round-trips it without inventing or dropping a field. Cheap, and it is the direct net under the 853-edge class. The cost is that the corpus must be curated or it becomes 74 fixtures.
(b) THE OLD BINARY AGAINST THE NEW DOCUMENT — the actual direction of the reported defect, and the harder one, because it needs a released binary downloaded in CI. Worth it only if the answer is "a server behind its record says so", which is what the fix already claims.
(c) TEST THE THING THAT SHIPS, NOT THE CRATE — run a subset of the gates against the published container image and the one-liner install, not against the working tree. NOTE: this is already written down as an unsatisfied requirement of its own, so option (c) is not a new idea, it is an existing one nobody has delivered.
(d) A FIELD-DEFECT CORPUS: every defect a consuming project reports becomes a permanent fixture, by rule. This is close to what already happens by hand — many gates exist because one project hit one thing — but it is a convention with no instrument, and the design already reports fixes whose cause was never recorded.

THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT: (a) and (c) are clearly worth their cost; (b) doubles CI's dependency surface by downloading a published release into the build, and a corpus of old exports is a maintenance burden that grows with every schema change. The restraint version is (a) with THREE fixtures and a stated rule for retiring them.
properties.name: OPEN — what regression corpus guards the UPGRADE path? Every gate today runs this commit's binary against this commit's data, and the defects users actually report are old-data-meets-new-binary
properties.rationale: Recorded open because the four options differ in cost by an order of magnitude and one of them (c) is already an unsatisfied requirement, which means part of the answer is "deliver what is written down" rather than "decide something new". The evidence is field reports from four consuming projects, not reasoning about what might break.
